source.title: Polycyclic Codes Associated with Trinomials: Good Codes and Open Questions

accepted.question_text: Let t1(x) = x^n - a x^i - b and t2(x) = x^n - a' x^(n-i) - b' be trinomials over a finite field F_q with the same order, meaning Ord(t1(x)) = Ord(t2(x)). If C1 is the family of all length-n polycyclic codes over F_q associated with t1(x), and C2 is the family of all length-n polycyclic codes over F_q associated with t2(x), is there always a one-to-one correspondence between C1 and C2 such that each code in one family corresponds to an equivalent code in the other family?
accepted.context_brief: equivalence of code families for equal-order reciprocal-style trinomials

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.5. Let t1pxq = x^n - axi - b, t2pxq = x^n - a' x^(n-i) - b' P Fq[x] be such that Ord(t1(x)) = Ord(t2(x)). Let C1 be the set of all polycyclic codes of length n over Fq associated with t1(x) and C2 be the set of all polycyclic codes of length n over Fq associated with t2(x). Then C1 and C2 are in a one-to-one correspondence where corresponding codes are equivalent to each other.

accepted.question_text: Suppose C is a polycyclic code over a finite field F_q whose associate trinomial is x^n - a x^i - b, and suppose its generator polynomial g(x) divides x^n - a x^i - b and also satisfies g(x)^2 = x^n - a x^i - b. Must C always be iso-dual, that is, equivalent to its Euclidean dual code?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1. If a polycyclic code C is generated by g(x)|x^n - axi - b and g^2(x) = x^n - axi - b, then C is isodual.

accepted.question_text: Over the binary field F_2, let C be a polycyclic code associated with the trinomial x^n - a x^i - b and generated by a divisor g(x) of that trinomial. Is C iso-dual if and only if g(x)^2 = x^n - a x^i - b?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2. Over F2, a polycyclic code C generated by g(x)|x^n - axi - b is iso-dual if and only if g^2(x) = x^n - axi - b.

accepted.question_text: Over a finite field GF(q), are the following families of polycyclic codes always iso-dual? First, when q is a power of an odd prime, a polycyclic code associated with the trinomial x^(2m) ± 2c x^m + c^2 and generated by g(x) = ±x^m ± c. Second, when q is a power of 2, a polycyclic code associated with the trinomial x^(2m) + a^2 x^(2i) + b^2 and generated by g(x) = x^m + a x^i + b.
accepted.context_brief: parametric families conjectured to be iso-dual

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.5. Over GF(q), • If q is a power of an odd prime, a polycyclic code associated with trinomial x^(2m) ± 2cx^m + c^2 and generated by g(x) = ±x^m ± c is isodual. • If q is a power of 2, a polycyclic code associated with the trinomial x^(2m) + a^2x^(2i) + b^2 and generated by g(x) = x^m + axi + b is isodual.

accepted.question_text: Is a polycyclic code over a finite field F_q self-dual exactly in the following situation: its generator polynomial has the form g(x) = x^m - a, it divides a trinomial x^(2m) - b x^m - c, and the scalar a satisfies a^2 = q - 1? In addition, if such a self-dual polycyclic code exists, must its minimum distance always be 2, and must every self-dual polycyclic code of this kind in fact be constacyclic rather than genuinely more general polycyclic?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.7. A polycyclic code over Fq is self-dual if and only if its generator is in the form g = x^m - a|x^(2m) - bx^m - c, where a^2 = q - 1. Also, the minimum distance of all self-dual polycyclic codes is 2 and they are all actually constacyclic codes.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist any binary polycyclic codes that are self-dual, self-orthogonal, or dual-containing, or are all three phenomena impossible over the field F_2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.10. There is no self-dual or self-orthogonal or dual-containing polycyclic codes over the binary field.

accepted.question_text: Let C be a polycyclic code whose generator polynomial g(x) divides a trinomial x^n - a x^i - b over a finite field, with n prime. Is it always true that C cannot be dual-containing?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.11. A polycyclic code is not dual-containing if the generator polynomial g|x^n - axi - b, where n is prime.

trace.notes: Mapped the PDF structure and found the explicit open-problem cluster on pages 8-12 in Sections 3 and 4; the paper contains no dedicated open-problems section but does contain seven labeled conjectures.

Introduction announces that some generated algebra problems are left as conjectures or open problems, which guided extraction toward the conjecture-labeled statements rather than the generic background open problems in coding theory.
Extracted the explicit labeled conjecture at the end of Section 3.
Extracted the first iso-duality conjecture from Section 4.1.
Extracted the binary-field iso-duality conjecture from Section 4.1.
Extracted the two-family isoduality conjecture following the trinomial square-root theorems.
Extracted the self-duality classification conjecture from Section 4.2.
Extracted the binary nonexistence conjecture from Section 4.2.
Extracted the prime-length dual-containing conjecture from Section 4.2.
Expanded the conjecture so that the order condition, the two trinomial families, and the equivalence claim are explicit in one standalone question.
Inlined the meanings of the associate trinomial and iso-duality claim without adding unsupported hypotheses.
Made the binary-field iff statement self-contained by stating the ambient field and divisor condition directly.
Kept both parameter families in a single accepted item because they are presented together as one labeled conjecture.
Expanded the classification conjecture to state both the structural iff claim and the additional minimum-distance and constacyclicity assertions.
Rewrote the ternary list of forbidden properties into one direct existence question over F_2.
Expanded the statement to specify the prime-length hypothesis and the divisor relation defining the code family.

No near-duplicate conjectures were merged; each labeled conjecture in Sections 3-4 was kept as a separate canonical item, except Conjecture 4.5 which naturally contains two subfamilies in one source-labeled conjecture.
Accepted items all have verbatim page-cited evidence, no unresolved cross-references, and no added facts beyond the source statements and directly supported ambient definitions.
